newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees record 97/98 Brazil orange juice output.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees record 97/98 Brazil orange juice output.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday forecast Brazil's 1997/1998 orange juice production would be a record 1.22 million tonnes, based on the expected large orange crop.
USDA pegged Brazil orange juice exports in marketing year 1997/98 (July-June) at 1.16 million tonnes, two percent above a a revised 1996/97 export forecast of 1.14 million tonnes.
USDA said the 1996/97 Brazilian FCOJ export forecast was revised upward based on higher exports to date than expected.
Juice yields in 1997/98 were forecast to approximate last year's levels, the department said.
USDA said Sao Paulo's oranges for processing in 1997/98 are forecast to increase to a record 295 million boxes, 10 percent above the 1996/97 estimate based on the expected larger harvest.
USDA said trade sources' orange processing forecasts ranged between 280 and 295 million boxes.

"Some sources indicate the size of the 1997/98 Florida orange crop and the condition of the September bloom for the 1998/99 Sao Paulo orange crop will have an impact on how many oranges will actually be processed in 1997/98," the department said.
The department will release its first forecast of the 1997/98 Florida orange crop in October.
USDA quoted trade sources saying that Brazil's processing season would be shorter in 1997/98 because of the big bloom in September/October.
The department said it would have more information about orange juice forecasts based on recent USDA travel to Brazil in a July trade and U.S export report.
